originality.rationale: The claim is a finite-field form classification of the classical nonzero cyclic permutation family. The closest 2013 source proves collapse to unit weights in its complex setting; later cycle-decomposition and graph-automorphism results do not give the finite-field residue invariant or class count. A 2023 paper gives an ambient finite-field orbit framework for all idempotent evolution algebras, but the inspected material does not state this support-conditioned all-dimensional formula. The residual risk from that inaccessible specialization is explicitly retained.

value.rationale: A nonzero directed cycle is the irreducible building block in the classical permutation-evolution family, and the historical complex theorem removes all weights by root extraction. Determining exactly what survives over finite fields is therefore a natural descent/moduli problem. The result gives a complete invariant, exact class count for all dimensions and finite fields, and exact automorphism orders, with a sharp criterion for when the classical collapse remains valid.
